report:
Short answer
- There is a clear, localisable difference: the B−A signal is concentrated almost entirely at the first token position (pos0) across many layers.  
- The content of that signal (from the logit-lens top tokens) shifts toward words about tragic/serious events, legal/medical contexts, and shock in the higher layers (examples: "tragic", "tragedy", "law", "surgeon", "clinic", "rescue", "corpses", "shocked", "blitz", "coming"). So Model B appears to have an increased initial-position residual activation that pushes the model toward those kinds of tokens relative to Model A.

Evidence and reasoning
- Norms: almost all of the L2 difference is at pos0 (very small norms at pos1–pos4, huge values at pos0 from layer 4 upward, peaking in late layers). That indicates the checkpoint difference mainly changes how the models represent the first token (the sequence-start / identity token) rather than mid-sequence processing.
- Logit-lens tokens: low-to-mid layers show varied nouns (e.g. "bottle", "Author"), but from roughly layer ~13 onward the top-scoring tokens include many semantically consistent tokens around serious/negative news-like themes: "rejected", "normal", then later "tragic", "tragedy", "law", "surgeon", "clinic", "downturn", "rescue", "corpses", "shocked", "blitz", "coming", etc. The repeated emergence of these tokens in higher layers supports an interpretable shift in the kind of concepts encoded at pos0.

What I cannot reliably claim
- I cannot definitively name a specific training objective (e.g., "safety tuning for violent content" or "news-domain fine-tuning") from this evidence alone. The pattern strongly suggests a change in the prior/initial-token bias toward serious/tragic/legal/medical topics, but that could arise from multiple causes (dataset shift, fine-tuning on certain corpora, or even tokenisation/embedding differences). Patchscope continuations were not available here (or not shown), which would have helped confirm how this pos0 shift affects full-generation behavior.

Concluding statement
- The interpretable difference is: Model B (relative to A) increases an initial-position residual component that nudges decoding toward tokens associated with tragedy/serious events and legal/medical contexts. The evidence supports this positional-and-semantic description but does not uniquely identify a specific training objective responsible for it.
